greeting.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
text: You're the fourth company through this month and the first that walked in facing the room. I notice things like that. It's most of my trade.
Sit down before you're counted. Everyone in here is counting, including the man pretending to be asleep.
New boots, old scabbard. That's a company that spends on the walking and not the killing. Sensible.

options.text: What are the other three doing?
You're sat where you can see both doors and neither window. You're waiting for somebody.

again.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
text: Still the same table. He's still late. I'm beginning to take it personally.
You came back with the same number of arms. That puts you above three of the four companies I've watched leave.
I've been hearing about you between drinks. Some of it was even about this valley.

options.text: What are they saying about us?

the_others.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
the_others.text: Two went up the cut road and came back thinner. The third didn't come back and nobody's gone to look.

for_coin.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
for_coin.text: For coin, for a roof, for a reason. Mostly the reason. Coin I can get anywhere and roofs are cheap this year.

caught_out.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
caught_out.text: ...I am. He's late. If he stays late, I'm free, and if I'm free you'll want to hear my price before somebody worse offers me theirs.

shrugged_off.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
shrugged_off.text: I'm sat where the fire is. Read that however you want, it'll still be warm.

the_drink.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
the_drink.text: Generous. That buys you one true thing: don't camp on the cut road. Camp off it, and don't light anything.

the_price.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
the_price.text: More than you have and less than you think. I'm not for sale today. Ask me on a day I've been insulted.

what_they_say.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
text: That you finish things. In this trade that's not praise, it's a price.
That somebody paid you and you did the work anyway. Nobody can decide if that's stupid or dangerous.
Two men argued about your name last night. Neither had met you. That's how it starts.

he_came.speaker: Tem the Sword Monkey
he_came.text: He came, saw you'd been sitting where I was, and left again. So whatever you are, he already knows. I'd think about that on the road.
